report.answer_text:
The five daily obligatory prayers (Salah) in Islam are:
1. Fajr: the dawn prayer, performed before sunrise. It has 2 rak'ahs (units of prayer).
2. Dhuhr: the midday prayer, performed after the sun passes its highest point. It has 4 rak'ahs.
3. Asr: the afternoon prayer. It has 4 rak'ahs.
4. Maghrib: the sunset prayer, performed just after the sun sets. It has 3 rak'ahs.
5. Isha: the night prayer, performed after twilight has faded. It has 4 rak'ahs.
Salah is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. Muslims perform these prayers facing the Kaaba in Mecca, after ritual purification (wudu). Friday congregational prayer (Jumu'ah) takes the place of Dhuhr for men on Fridays.
The number of rak'ahs given here is for the obligatory (fard) portions. Many Muslims also pray additional voluntary (sunnah) rak'ahs, and some schools of thought treat the Witr prayer after Isha as especially emphasized or even required. Exact prayer times vary by location and time of year.
